records.title: Point
records.definition: A point represents a precise location in geometry without length, width or thickness.
principles: Points can be used to define geometric structures.
relationships: Points form lines, shapes and coordinate systems.
misconceptions: A drawn dot is a representation of a mathematical point.
assessment_ideas: Plot points on a coordinate plane.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard geometry definitions

records.title: Angle
records.definition: An angle describes the amount of rotation between two rays sharing a common endpoint.
principles: A full rotation is 360 degrees or 2pi radians.
relationships: Angles occur in triangles, polygons, circles and trigonometry.
misconceptions: An angle represents more than just the visible space between lines.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard geometry definitions

records.title: Triangle
records.definition: A triangle is a polygon with three sides and three interior angles.
principles: The interior angles of a Euclidean triangle sum to 180 degrees.
relationships: Triangles are fundamental to geometry and trigonometry.
misconceptions: Triangles do not need to have equal sides.
assessment_ideas: Classify triangles using sides and angles.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard Euclidean geometry

records.title: Circle
records.definition: A circle is the set of points in a plane that are the same distance from a fixed centre.
principles: Area is pi times radius squared.
relationships: Circles connect geometry, trigonometry and coordinate geometry.
misconceptions: Radius and diameter are not the same length.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard Euclidean geometry

records.title: Data
records.definition: Data are recorded observations, measurements or values collected for analysis or decision-making.
principles: Statistical conclusions depend on the quality and relevance of data.
relationships: Data are central to statistics, science, research and computing.
misconceptions: More data does not automatically mean better data.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard statistical definitions

records.title: Arithmetic Mean
records.definition: The arithmetic mean is the sum of numerical observations divided by the number of observations.
principles: Mean equals total value divided by the number of observations.
relationships: Mean is a measure of central tendency alongside median and mode.
misconceptions: The mean does not have to be one of the observed values.
questions: How is the arithmetic mean calculated?
assessment_ideas: Calculate and interpret a dataset mean.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard statistical definitions

records.title: Probability
records.definition: Probability is a numerical measure of how likely an event is to occur.
principles: Probability ranges from 0 to 1 in the standard model.
Impossible events have probability 0 and certain events have probability 1.
relationships: Probability connects mathematics with statistics, risk and decision-making.
examples: A fair coin has probability 1/2 of landing heads.
misconceptions: A probability of 1/2 does not guarantee exactly half of a small number of trials.
sources: Dream Education original synthesis; standard probability theory
